function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Here’s a quick rundown of the most common ways to get a cake delivered (or pick it up) so you can choose what fits your needs best: | Option | How it works | Pros | Cons | |--------|--------------|------|------| | **Local bakeries** (e.g., *The Sweet Spot*, *Baker & Co.*) | Search “cake shop near me” → visit their website or call. Many have online ordering forms or accept phone orders. | • Fresh, often custom‑made.
• You can see photos, read reviews, and sometimes even taste samples. | • Limited to your city or region.
• May charge extra for delivery or pickup fees. | | **National chain bakeries** (e.g., *Panera Bread*, *Cinnabon*, *Krispy Kreme*) | Order through their app or website; they usually offer delivery via their own service or through third‑party apps. | • Reliable quality standards.
• Often have loyalty programs. | • Less variety than independent shops.
• Delivery windows may be longer. | | **Online marketplaces** (e.g., *Etsy*, *Amazon Handmade*) | Browse sellers who specialize in cakes; many ship nationwide. | • Huge selection of unique designs.
• Ability to customize colors, flavors, and messages. | • Shipping costs can add up.
• Delivery times vary by seller. | | **Food‑delivery platforms** (e.g., *Uber Eats*, *DoorDash*, *Postmates*, *Grubhub*) | Search “cakes” or “bakeries” in the app; place an order from a nearby shop that partners with the platform. | • Convenient, same‑day delivery.
• Track status in real time. | • Delivery fee + tip.
• Some shops only allow pickup. | | **Grocery‑store delivery** (e.g., *Instacart*, *Shipt*, *Amazon Fresh*) | Add a cake to your grocery cart; the driver picks it up at the store and delivers. | • One‑stop shopping for groceries + cake.
• Usually free delivery for premium members. | • Cake selection limited to store inventory.
• Delivery window may be less flexible. | | **Specialty cake shops** (e.g., *Cake Boss*, *Charmed Cakes*, *Sweet Treats Bakery*) | These shops often have dedicated e‑commerce sites and may partner with local couriers. | • Custom design services.
• High‑quality ingredients. | • Prices can be higher.
• Delivery may require scheduling. | ### Quick Tips for Ordering 1. **Know Your Delivery Area** – Check each site’s delivery map or enter your ZIP code to confirm coverage. 2. **Read Reviews** – Look at recent ratings on Google, Yelp, or the platform itself. 3. **Check Delivery Fees** – Some services waive fees for orders over a certain amount or for premium memberships. 4. **Ask About Allergens** – If you’re ordering for someone with dietary restrictions, confirm ingredient lists. 5. **Schedule Ahead** – For birthdays or events, place orders at least 24–48 hours in advance to guarantee availability. ### Where to Start? If you’re looking for something quick and local, try searching “cake shop near me” on Google Maps or Yelp. If you want a custom design or a specific flavor profile, Etsy or a specialty cake shop’s own website is a great place to browse portfolios. For same‑day convenience, open your favorite food‑delivery app and search “cakes” or “bakeries.” Let me know if you’d like recommendations tailored to a particular city or if you have a specific occasion in mind—happy to narrow it down!
